findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the new job `name:` the collapsed loop job will carry in `_optionality.yml` (e.g. `optionality / venv-loop`) and add a corresponding AC: 'main-protection.snapshot.json contains exactly that check name and no others from this workflow that were removed'.
evidence: 'it IS POSTed back by infra/github/rollback-mirror-lock.sh:75-88 — so leaving it stale means an emergency rollback would demand checks that cannot exist and would freeze main'
AC only says 'no longer names removed checks' — it specifies what to REMOVE but not what to INSERT as the replacement check name for the new single-loop job
The new job's `name:` key in `_optionality.yml` is never stated in the plan, so the resulting GitHub Actions status-check string is unknowable from the plan text alone
findings.finding: The plan instructs the executor to update `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` to remove the old per-matrix check names, but never states what the NEW job name (and therefore new GitHub Actions check name) the collapsed single-job will emit. Because `rollback-mirror-lock.sh:75-88` POSTs this snapshot back verbatim to re-arm the branch protection, an incorrectly populated snapshot can either (a) freeze `main` by requiring checks that don't exist, or (b) silently drop the new check from required status — both consequences the plan calls out as critical yet doesn't close.
findings.location: Scope section — `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json` bullet; AC: 'infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json no longer names removed checks'
scenarios: Executor renames the job arbitrarily; snapshot gets the wrong string; rollback fires and freezes main
Executor removes old entries but adds nothing; required-status-checks list shrinks silently; the new loop job is no longer gating
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Scope bullet: 'The new job will be named `optionality / venv-loop`; update the snapshot to replace the six removed entries with this single entry.' Then add or amend the AC to: 'infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json removes the six old per-matrix check names and adds exactly `optionality / venv-loop`.'

The Scope section explains the snapshot is POSTed by `rollback-mirror-lock.sh` during emergencies; if the new single-job check name is absent from the snapshot after the update, an emergency rollback would POST a ruleset that omits the new required check, silently weakening the gate.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC11; Scope section (infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json paragraph)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving command for the byte-identical AC, e.g. a parity test that hashes or textually compares the `clean-core-wheel` job block before and after, or a note that `git diff` on that block is the verification step.
evidence: AC states 'byte-identical' but the Testing section and the rest of the ACs provide no corresponding proving command for this specific claim
The other structural ACs are backed by `pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py`, but no test is described that asserts the wheel job is unchanged
findings.finding: The AC 'clean-core-wheel is byte-identical to its current form' has no proving command. The plan never states HOW to verify byte-identity (e.g., `git diff -- .github/workflows/_optionality.yml` scoped to the wheel job block, or a hash comparison). Without a concrete command, an executor who accidentally edits the wheel job section has no deterministic in-session check to catch the regression.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'clean-core-wheel is byte-identical to its current form'
scenarios: Executor inadvertently touches the clean-core-wheel job during refactoring; no automated guard catches it; the only lane where agents_extra_installed() is False silently changes
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Testing section: 'A parity test in `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` extracts the `clean-core-wheel` job block from the workflow YAML and asserts it is unchanged from the committed reference hash/text.' Alternatively, state: 'Verify with `git diff HEAD .github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — the `clean-core-wheel` job block must show no diff lines.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the policy for which extras belong in the union set (e.g., a comment in `_optionality.yml` and in the parity test), and add a test assertion or code comment that makes the union set's composition reviewable when `_optional.EXTRAS` changes.
evidence: "A UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly into one venv."
The test guards only that the loop covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`, not that the union set policy is consistent.
No explanation of why `grounding` and `metrics` are excluded from the union, nor where this policy is documented.
findings.finding: The plan hardcodes `.[agents,eval,tracing]` as the UNION set, which is a subset of `_optional.EXTRAS` (`{agents,eval,grounding,metrics,tracing}`), but provides no policy statement, no configurable definition, and no test guard explaining why these three (not all five) form the union — meaning a future contributor adding an extra to `_optional.EXTRAS` will have no signal that the union set may also need updating.
findings.location: Approach section ('A UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly') / AC line: 'A UNION iteration installs `.[agents,eval,tracing]` jointly'
scenarios: A new extra is added to `_optional.EXTRAS`; the loop test passes (it only checks isolation coverage) but the union set silently stays stale, missing joint-resolution testing for the new extra.
A developer wonders whether to include a new heavy extra in the union and has no documented decision criterion to follow.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a comment in `_optionality.yml` and in `test_ci_workflow_parity.py`: `# Union covers extras with known transitive-dependency overlap (agents/eval/tracing); grounding and metrics are standalone. Update this set when adding extras with shared heavy deps.` and assert in the test that the union set is a subset of `_optional.EXTRAS` keys (to catch typos).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan for the workflow job replacement (e.g., document the `git revert` commit procedure, or use an expand-contract sequence: add the new loop job alongside the old matrix jobs first, verify it passes, then remove the old jobs in a second commit).
evidence: "Collapse the 5 `per-extra` cells + `union` into ONE job running a venv loop."
No mention of expand-contract (add new job, verify, then remove old) or of how to revert if the loop job is faulty.
The plan describes testing via a scratch-branch push, but does not specify what happens if that test reveals a broken job — there is no stated back-out sequence.
findings.finding: The plan replaces the existing per-extra matrix jobs and union job with no expand-contract sequence and no explicit rollback path for the workflow change itself. If the new venv-loop job is pushed and broken, the old job names are gone and the Verified gate is broken with no described recovery path (beyond `git revert`, which is unmentioned).
scenarios: Scratch-branch test is skipped or passes for wrong reasons; broken job is merged; Verified gate on main is now broken with no quick path back.
A regression is introduced in a follow-up PR; reverting the workflow requires knowing the exact old matrix structure which is no longer documented in the plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Rollback' section: 'If the loop job is found broken after merge, revert commit <sha> (the _optionality.yml change). The snapshot rollback-script update must also be reverted atomically (same PR or same revert commit) to keep the two files consistent.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly verify (with a cite to the caller workflow files) that no calling workflow sets PYTHONPATH or PIP_* at workflow/job scope; alternatively, add an explicit `env: PYTHONPATH: ''` guard on the venv-loop step itself so the isolation contract is self-enforcing rather than environment-dependent.
evidence: Plan quote: 'PYTHONPATH/PIP_* are unset in both workflows, so --copies/PYTHONNOUSERSITE/--without-pip are NOT needed.'
No citation to optionality.yml, gerrit-verify.yaml, or optionality.yml (the push-lane caller) is given to ground this claim.
Python venv docs confirm PYTHONPATH is NOT cleared by venv creation or absolute-path invocation — it is inherited by child processes unless explicitly unset.
The existing _optionality.yml (read from repo) has no top-level env: block, but callers are not shown in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'PYTHONPATH/PIP_* are unset in both workflows' as the justification for skipping PYTHONNOUSERSITE/--copies, but provides no citation to the calling workflow files to verify this. If any calling workflow (optionality.yml, gerrit-verify.yaml) or a future edit introduces a PYTHONPATH env var — even scoped to a different step — the venv isolation contract of the loop silently weakens: the ambient PYTHONPATH leaks into every '$v/bin/python' subprocess because venv activation does not clear it.
findings.location: Approach section, 'VENV HYGIENE' paragraph: "PYTHONPATH/PIP_* are unset in both workflows, so --copies/PYTHONNOUSERSITE/--without-pip are NOT needed."
scenarios: A future caller workflow adds 'env: PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/src' (e.g., for a different job), and the venv-loop job inherits it, allowing the ambient src/ to shadow the venv's installed package — an iteration could pass while actually testing the wrong install.
A Dependabot or teammate PR adds a workflow-level PYTHONPATH for an unrelated step; the optionality loop silently loses isolation with no lint or test catching it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `env:\n  PYTHONPATH: ''\n  PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV: ''` to the venv-loop step's `env:` block in `_optionality.yml`. This makes isolation self-enforcing regardless of what callers set, eliminating the need for the unverified environmental assumption.

findings.finding: The Approach explicitly enumerates exactly 5 isolation extras ('agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding') for the venv loop, but AC #9 requires 'every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`' to appear in the looped extra list — and the Approach itself acknowledges that `metrics` is already in `_optional.EXTRAS` with zero CI coverage. An implementer following the Approach would write a 5-iteration loop and fail AC #9; an implementer satisfying AC #9 would need to add a `metrics` (and potentially other) iteration but has no guidance from the Approach on its behavior (no `rebar-mcp`-style special case, no described assertions).
findings.location: Approach §2 ('Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)') vs. Acceptance Criteria #9 ('every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`') vs. Testing §3 ('today `metrics` is in `_optional.EXTRAS` with no per-extra coverage, and `pyproject.toml` declares eleven extras against the five covered')
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, change 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)' to 'Six ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding, metrics)' and add a brief note that the metrics iteration runs `import rebar` + `_optional.extra_installed('metrics')` only (no console-script equivalent to rebar-mcp). Then update AC #9 to match. Alternatively, if metrics is intentionally deferred, narrow AC #9 to 'every extra whose package is installable in CI' and document the exclusion explicitly.

findings.finding: The Approach section enumerates exactly five venv loop iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding) but `_optional.EXTRAS` has five keys (agents, eval, tracing, grounding, metrics) — `metrics` is in `EXTRAS` and has no loop coverage, while `mcp` is NOT in `EXTRAS`. AC9 requires the loop to cover every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`. As written, the loop body in the Approach section does NOT satisfy AC9: metrics is uncovered, and the AC9 guard test (asserting every EXTRAS key appears in the loop list) would fail against the described implementation.
findings.location: Approach §2 (loop extras list) vs. AC9 / Testing §3
findings.suggested_fix: Add `metrics` as a sixth isolation iteration (making the loop seven total iterations including union), and update the Approach section to read 'Six ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding, metrics)'. Alternatively, if metrics is intentionally excluded from isolation CI (e.g. because lizard is heavy), add a documented exception in the AC9 guard and explain in the Testing section.

findings.finding: The Approach section specifies five isolation extras [agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding], but `src/rebar/_optional.py:34-48` shows `_optional.EXTRAS` contains {agents, eval, tracing, grounding, metrics} — `mcp` is absent and `metrics` is present. AC #9 and the new test guard both require the looped extra list to cover every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`. An implementer following the Approach literally would write a loop over the stated five extras and the new guard test would immediately fail (metrics uncovered, mcp not in EXTRAS).
findings.location: Approach §2 — 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)'; AC #9; src/rebar/_optional.py:34-48
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, replace 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)' with: 'Five ISOLATION iterations for the five `_optional.EXTRAS` keys (agents, eval, tracing, grounding, metrics), each asserting `_optional.extra_installed(extra)`; plus a sixth MCP iteration (extra="mcp") that installs `.[mcp]` and runs `$v/bin/rebar-mcp --help` only (mcp has no EXTRAS probe). The UNION iteration remains a seventh step, giving seven total iterations in the loop.' Update AC items 1-3 and #9 to reflect this corrected count and structure.

findings.finding: The plan describes a six-iteration loop covering 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)' but `metrics` is a concrete key in `_optional.EXTRAS` (src/rebar/_optional.py:34-48) and is absent from the loop list. The plan simultaneously states AC: 'assert every extra in `_optional.EXTRAS` appears in the looped extra list' — this guard would FAIL on the loop as described, since `metrics` ∈ `_optional.EXTRAS` but ∉ {agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding}. The plan acknowledges `metrics` is in `_optional.EXTRAS` with no per-extra coverage, but never resolves whether it should be added to the loop or exempted from the AC guard and why.
findings.location: Approach / '2. Collapse the 5 per-extra cells' section; AC item 9 ('A checked-in test asserts the looped extra list covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`')
findings.suggested_fix: Either add `metrics` to the loop's extra list (a sixth isolation iteration becomes a seventh) so the AC9 guard passes without modification, or rewrite AC9 as 'assert every extra in `_optional.EXTRAS` THAT IS in the loop list covers every key in `_optional.EXTRAS` ∩ LOOP' and document why metrics is excluded.

findings.finding: The plan's Approach section enumerates the venv loop as 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)' — but `src/rebar/_optional.py:47` shows `metrics` is a concrete key in `_optional.EXTRAS` (probe: `lizard`) that the plan's loop omits. The plan's own AC #9 requires the loop to cover every key in `_optional.EXTRAS`, so implementing the approach as written would fail AC #9: `metrics` would be in `_optional.EXTRAS` but absent from the loop.
findings.location: Approach § '2. Collapse the 5 per-extra cells + union into ONE job' — 'Five ISOLATION iterations (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `metrics` iteration to the six-iteration loop (making it seven iterations), installing `.[metrics]` into its own venv, running `import rebar` and asserting `_optional.extra_installed('metrics')` — parallel to the other `_optional.EXTRAS` members. This resolves the contradiction between the Approach enumeration and AC #9.

findings.finding: The plan's six-iteration loop enumerates five isolation extras (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding) but omits `metrics`, which is a concrete entry in `_optional.EXTRAS` (src/rebar/_optional.py line 47: `"metrics": ("lizard", "code-health metrics analyzers")`) with a pip extra in pyproject.toml (line 156: `metrics = ["lizard>=1.23"]`). AC3 says 'for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, assert `extra_installed(extra)`', but there is no isolation venv iteration for `metrics` in the proposed loop. The omission appears to be inherited from the existing matrix (which also lacks `metrics`) rather than derived from a symbol-graph lookup of `_optional.EXTRAS` keys.
findings.location: Approach section — 'five ISOLATION iterations, one per extra (agents, eval, tracing, mcp, grounding)'; AC3 — 'for extras in `_optional.EXTRAS`, assert `_optional.extra_installed(extra)`'
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the loop's extras by iterating `python -c 'from rebar._optional import EXTRAS; print(list(EXTRAS))'` to get the ground-truth list from the symbol graph, then add `metrics` as a seventh iteration (no boot-check equivalent to `rebar-mcp --help` exists for it; the `extra_installed` assertion via EXTRAS is sufficient).

findings.finding: The plan bundles two self-described 'independent reductions' that are each independently valuable, testable, and releasable: (1) delete import-linter + add durable collection guards, and (2) collapse per-extra matrix + union into a venv-loop job + update snapshot JSON. Reduction 2 alone is sufficient to get under the 20-slot org limit (21-6 = 15 slots), so Reduction 1 is not a prerequisite. Bundling them increases blast radius and makes bisection harder if the venv-loop bash logic introduces a regression.
